slides.headline: Around 80 games are hidden in this painting. How many did you play?
slides.sub: Pieter Bruegel the Elder, Children's Games, 1560

slides.headline: Flanders, 1560
slides.text: Bruegel hands an entire town over to its children. Streets, windows, even the river: all full of games.

slides.headline: Start bottom left
slides.text: Two girls play knucklebones with little bones. Today we call it jacks.

slides.headline: Then, hoops
slides.text: Right behind them, kids race wooden hoops across the square, pushing them with sticks.

slides.headline: Next, leapfrog
slides.text: One boy vaults over another's back. 460 years later, every schoolyard still plays it.

slides.headline: Meanwhile, by the fence
slides.text: A boy stands on his head, legs in the air. Some things never change.

slides.headline: Further up, stilts
slides.text: Short stilts, tall stilts, and kids proudly towering over everyone.

slides.headline: And in the middle of it all
slides.text: A pretend wedding procession. The children are playing at being grown-ups.

slides.headline: Even far away
slides.text: The river in the distance is full of kids swimming. Which of these games did you play most?
